validity.recommendation: No structural fix needed. Existence, routing and classification are solidly corroborated; see the two separate spec flags below (StartYear1 and Capacity attribution) and the attribution flag on EndLocation.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented line, not a GEM-only entity. Multiple independent sources describe the 84km Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh corridor as built with TWO parallel 530mm lines ('нитки') plus a later, separate 3rd (720mm, then a brand-new Dec-2024 84km replacement/addition): neftegaz.ru's 2021 federal-budget article (699520) states explicitly 'физический износ 1-й нитки труб составляет 100%, 2-й — 65%' (wear of line-1 pipes = 100%, line-2 = 65%) -- direct, itemized proof that TWO physically distinct 530mm pipes exist on this corridor, not one. neftegaz.ru's field-reference page (671733) and explosion article (194257), ipng.ysn.ru's 2021 parliamentary-panel article, and (via Wayback, live URL is a JS anti-bot shell) interfax-russia.ru's Rostekhnadzor-violations article (2023) and State Duma funding article (2021) all corroborate the corridor and its operator. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct -- the Rostekhnadzor article explicitly names 'Участок магистрального газопровода СВГКМ-Мастах-Берге-Якутск (I, II, и III нитки)' (trunk-gas-pipeline section ... lines I, II and III), i.e. it names THIS row's own 'line II' directly as part of the regulated trunk asset. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 32-row roster and the 8-row Sakhatransneftegaz family: P6695 is 'String II' of the Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh segment, a sibling of P3365 ('String I', same 84km corridor, already worked in this batch -- see its shard) and distinct from P6694 (720mm/382km, a different, longer segment further down the corridor) and from P3361 (per P3365's own cross_row_leads, the brand-new December 2024 84km 'String III' launch on this same corridor). No relabel/segment-double-count risk found for P6695 itself.

validity.recommendation: Recommend removing/correcting StartYear1=2014 for this 530mm 'String II' row. An authoritative, government-press-service-sourced article (Interfax, read via Wayback since the live host bot-walls automated fetches) states explicitly that the first TWO lines of this system were commissioned 'late 1960s and 1980s respectively' -- i.e. this row (line 2 of 2) should read roughly '1980s', not 2014. 2014 is independently, solidly documented elsewhere in this GEM family as the commissioning year of a separate, newer 720mm THIRD line (matching sibling P6694's own recorded StartYear almost exactly -- see cross_row_leads), and P3365's own shard (this same batch) makes the identical finding for String I with 1967 as its proposed year. This strongly suggests a systematic cross-row date misattribution across the whole Sakhatransneftegaz family, not a one-off error. Flagging as a concern rather than auto-correcting: no source gives an exact year within the 1980s for String II specifically, only the decade.
validity.researcher_notes: Source: interfax-russia.ru's 2021 State Duma funding article (bot-walled live, read via Wayback capture 20211130114548) states: 'Первые две нитки газопровода Средневилюйское-Якутск по 460 км каждая были введены [в эксплуатацию в] конце 1960-х и 1980-х годов соответственно' (the first two lines of the Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk gas pipeline, 460km each, were commissioned in the late 1960s and the 1980s respectively). The same article states line 3 ('третья нитка') began construction in the early 2000s and is 384km -- matching P6694/P3361's spec discussion. Cross-checked against neftegaz.ru's 2021 federal-budget article (699520), which independently states the 84km Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh corridor's line 1 is 100% physically worn and line 2 is 65% worn as of 2021 -- consistent with line 2 (this row) being newer than line 1 but still decades-old (1980s), and utterly inconsistent with a 2014 in-service date (which would show near-zero wear by 2021, not 65%). I also checked aostng.ru/about/history/ (live page is empty/JS-rendered; a 2018 Wayback capture was read in full) for an exact year, but that page's history narrative covers the OTHER (Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk) corridor's 1967 commissioning and the still-under-construction (as of 2018) third line of THIS corridor -- it does not give an exact year for 'String II' specifically, only the general 1960s-80s buildout era already captured above. This satisfies independent corroboration for the wrongness of 2014 (interfax, government-sourced, vs. neftegaz's own internal consistency showing this GEM family's sibling P6694 legitimately owns the 2014 date) even though an exact replacement year is not pinned down.

validity.recommendation: Keep Capacity=1.50 bcm/y as recorded for now (it is within rounding of the source figure once converted), but this is now a CONFIRMED aggregate-double-counting risk, not just a hypothesis: sibling P3365 ('String I', same 84km corridor) independently carries the identical Capacity=1.50 bcm/y, sourced to the exact same 'combined' figure. No corrected per-string split figure is available to propose; recommend a targeted follow-up against a Sakhatransneftegaz/Glavgosexpertiza engineering document if a per-line split is ever needed.
validity.researcher_notes: neftegaz.ru's explosion article (194257) states 'Проектная производительность 2 х ниток - 4,2 млн м3/сутки, максимальная - 6,3 млн м3/сутки' (design capacity of the 2 [530mm] lines - 4.2 million m3/day, maximum 6.3 million m3/day) -- explicitly a COMBINED total for both 530mm strings together, not per-line. Converting: 4.2 million m3/day x 365 = 1,533 million m3/y = ~1.53 bcm/y, matching this row's recorded 1.50 bcm/y within rounding. Checking P3365's own already-completed shard (this batch) confirms my suspicion directly: P3365 ('String I') ALSO independently carries Capacity=1.50 bcm/y sourced to the identical combined figure -- meaning the same system-level total (~1.53 bcm/y) is very likely attributed to EACH of the two 530mm strings individually on the sheet, rather than being split between them (which would put each string closer to ~0.75 bcm/y if split evenly, though the two lines may not actually split capacity evenly given their differing wear/age). No source gives the two strings' capacities separately.
